items.title: Daily COVID-19 Brief: Issue 62
items.snippet_en: United Church of Christ published on July 6, 2020, that the idea of 5G networks causing COVID-19 is a myth. They cite ICNIRP, WHO, CDC, and FEMA, stating 5G electromagnetic fields cannot carry viruses and infection requires physical contact.

items.title: ITU statement on 5G and COVID-19
items.snippet_en: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a UN agency, confirmed on April 22, 2020, there is no scientific basis for claims linking 5G technology to COVID-19. Viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks, and COVID-19 spread in countries without 5G.

items.title: No link between 5G and COVID-19, UN agency confirms
items.snippet_en: The International Telecommunication Union (ITU), a UN agency, confirmed on April 22, 2020, there is no scientific basis for claims linking 5G technology to COVID-19. Viruses cannot travel on radio waves or mobile networks, and COVID-19 spread in countries without 5G.

items.title: 5G and coronavirus (COVID-19)
items.snippet_en: GOV.UK published on May 6, 2020, stating there is no evidence of a link between 5G and coronavirus. Scientific experts from WHO and fact-checking organizations like Full Fact have rejected these theories.

items.title: 5G Doesn’t Cause COVID-19, But the Rumor It Does Spreads Like a Virus
items.snippet_en: Boston University published on January 4, 2021, explaining that 5G technology emits low levels of radiation, not significantly different from 4G, and does not cause COVID-19. COVID-19 is a viral disease caused by SARS-CoV-2.

items.title: 5G and COVID-19 conspiracy theories
items.snippet_en: La Trobe University, in an article updated January 31, 2023, states there is no evidence that 5G radio frequencies cause or exacerbate the spread of coronavirus. Radiation and viruses are different phenomena and do not interact.

items.title: COVID-19 and 5G: A Statistical Analysis of the Correlation Between 5G Exposure and COVID-19 Cases and Deaths in the United States
items.snippet_en: A study published on April 12, 2021, found a statistically significant increase in COVID-19 cases and deaths in U.S. states and counties with 5G millimeter wave technology. States with 5G mmW technology had higher cases and deaths per million.

items.title: StatisticalProof.pdf
items.snippet_en: A study found a statistically significant increase in COVID-19 cases and deaths in U.S. states and counties with 5G millimeter wave technology. However, the model only explains 28.74% of the variability in cases, indicating other factors are involved.
